scope.selection: Later drafts outside reviewer34 first44/50-draft cutoff; three later VW and two Mazda articles, plus three new Escape AWD and two later Ford ignition/body-network articles.
scope.excluded: All unselected drafts and broader model applicability. Source checks establish support only for the exact selected article claims and cited workshop scope.

sourceChecks.locator: P Code Charts / P1568; illustrated VAG/SAE fault row and associated cause/action columns
Throttle Valve Control Module, Checking; Function, Test requirements, and Test sequence
ECM, Adapting to Throttle Valve Control Module; Function, Test requirements, and Test sequence

samples.method: Read complete article and cited original manufacturer chart image and/or complete manufacturer procedure transcription in locally retrieved public-mirror HTML.
factsChecked: Original chart image shows VAG 17976/J338 mechanical malfunction, separate from P1558 electrical drive malfunction; EPC footnote applies.
Adaptation learns emergency spring position and spring return, with ignition on and engine stopped; dirt/binding, low battery and wiring can interrupt it.
At least 11.5 V, coolant 5–95°C, closed throttle and no DTCs are adaptation prerequisites. Separate module check has opposite-direction G187/G188 feedback.
Source display group60 versus illustration80 conflict is disclosed, not converted into an invented scan sequence.

sourceChecks.locator: P Code Charts / P1477; illustrated VAG/SAE fault row and associated cause/action columns
Leak Detection Pump (LDP), Check; Function, Test requirements, and Test sequence
Output Diagnostic Test Mode Function 03; actuator sequence, AIR pump relay J299, N80, and V144 diagnostic branches

samples.method: Read complete article and cited original manufacturer chart image and/or complete manufacturer procedure transcription in locally retrieved public-mirror HTML.
factsChecked: Original chart image identifies VAG 17885 general V144 malfunction, not adjacent short-to-ground/B+ or insufficient-vacuum variants.
Output mode requires pump click and tests pulsed connector command before wiring/supply/controller decision.
Component test independently checks terminals 1–3 at 640–720 ohms and 2–3 at 17.5–27.5 ohms; article correctly avoids collapsing them to one pump value.
No unsupported leak-size threshold, fuel-cap diagnosis, failure likelihood or unsafe fuel-system intervention.

sourceChecks.locator: P Code Charts / P1749; illustrated VAG/SAE fault row and associated cause/action columns
Engine Control Module (ECM), Coding; Function, Test requirements, and Test sequence

samples.method: Read complete article and cited original manufacturer chart image and/or complete manufacturer procedure transcription in locally retrieved public-mirror HTML.
factsChecked: Original VAG 18157 image names invalid TCM coding and wrong or incorrectly coded ECM; actions explicitly check both modules.
ECM coding procedure requires five-digit vehicle-specific code and adopts displayed value after ignition is switched off.
Incorrect coding can cause driveability/shift behavior, false DTCs and omitted functions; no universal sample coding copied.

sourceChecks.locator: Normal Operation; U300D:11 trigger; L1 KEY_POS_4X4 versus KEY_STATUS_4X4 branches

samples.method: Read complete article and cited original manufacturer chart image and/or complete manufacturer procedure transcription in locally retrieved public-mirror HTML.
factsChecked: Exact suffix :11 is run/start input short to ground; code can set if ignition is not RUN during self-test.
Original normal-operation section identifies hardwired input plus BCM HS-CAN ignition position message.
L1 KEY_STATUS_4X4 mismatch leads to BJB fuse 54 (5 A)/CBB54; KEY_POS_4X4 mismatch leads to ignition-switch/steering-column diagnosis; article preserves the distinction.
No mechanical transfer-case conclusion or live-circuit bypass instructions.

sourceChecks.locator: Fault Trigger Conditions image; I10–I13 sense and accessory circuit short-to-voltage isolation; I16

samples.method: Read complete article and cited original manufacturer chart image and/or complete manufacturer procedure transcription in locally retrieved public-mirror HTML.
factsChecked: Original chart image explicitly assigns U3011:62 OFF signal-compare failure; IPC ignition status compared with direct start/stop input at RFA.
I9/I10 prioritize other IPC/RFA codes; I11 starter-sense short-to-voltage branch applies to U3011 while U3010 skips to I12.
I12/I13 accessory relay isolation distinguishes circuit voltage from relay contribution.

I16 connector check precedes RFA replacement; replacement requires configuration, PATS parameter reset and key programming. Article preserves professional boundary and makes no battery-drain-rate inference.

sourceChecks.locator: id140202300300, P0DF4:00 system malfunction location and detection condition; common ISG Diagnostic Procedure steps 1–4

samples.method: Read complete article and cited original manufacturer chart image and/or complete manufacturer procedure transcription in locally retrieved public-mirror HTML.
factsChecked: Original Mazda id140202300300 associates P0DF4:00 with internal FET temperature V-phase sensor characteristic malfunction.
Difference between microcomputer and stator driver-control IC inputs at least 0.2 V for continuous 1 s; comparison distinguished from absolute low/high thresholds.
Snapshot preservation, present/past distinction, ignition-on wait of at least 10 s and CAN diagnosis before conditional ISG replacement are retained.

Shared fail-safe inhibits assist, regeneration and i-stop and transfers 12 V loads to the 12 V battery; battery depletion warning supported. Wiring/connector fields are not applicable and article gives no internal probing instructions.

sourceChecks.locator: id140202300300, P0DF9:00 system malfunction location and detection condition; common ISG Diagnostic Procedure steps 1–4

samples.method: Read complete article and cited original manufacturer chart image and/or complete manufacturer procedure transcription in locally retrieved public-mirror HTML.
factsChecked: Original Mazda id140202300300 associates P0DF9:00 with W-phase high input, distinct from W-phase comparison P0DF7 and low-input P0DF8.
At least 2.95 V for continuous 0.5 s; electrical threshold is not converted into an unsupported temperature or overheating diagnosis.
Common recurrence/CAN procedure, communication-noise note and completion check for other DTCs accurately described.
Shared ISG safety boundary and fail-safe consequences retained without internal-electronics probing or owner road-test instructions.

sourceChecks.locator: Pinpoint Test A; four C0090 suffix triggers; motor circuit checks

samples.method: Read complete article and cited original manufacturer chart image and/or complete manufacturer procedure transcription in locally retrieved public-mirror HTML.
factsChecked: Original Ford Test A distinguishes :16 below 9 V during shift, :18 zero motor current commanded on, :19 current above 1 A at zero duty, and :71 absent cam/fork movement.
Article numerical claims concern :18/:19 and preserve command state; no invented current limit for the low-voltage suffix.
Reversible motor swaps power and ground by command; position-sensor faults take priority before the :71 stuck-actuator conclusion.
Open, ground-short and short-together circuit branches precede component decision. No actuator forcing or unsafe driveline operation instructed.

sourceChecks.locator: Pinpoint Tests C and M; fork signal duty/frequency and C0092:92 mechanical branch

samples.method: Read complete article and cited original manufacturer chart image and/or complete manufacturer procedure transcription in locally retrieved public-mirror HTML.
factsChecked: Original Tests C/B identify fork sensor B versus cam sensor A and shared power/return; companion C0091 leads to common-circuit diagnosis.
Fork duty below 10 percent or above 90 percent and frequency outside 1 kHz plus/minus 40 Hz; does not import cam sensor plus/minus 150 Hz tolerance.
Exact :92 routes to Test M learned-position/mechanical recurrence branch, not generic electrical branch.
Source C0092:17 trigger mislabels cam in one sentence; article follows fork header and does not propagate typo. Source road-test sequence is not turned into owner driving instructions.

sourceChecks.locator: Pinpoint Test H; C05F4:00 plausibility trigger; separate H7 performance route

samples.method: Read complete article and cited original manufacturer chart image and/or complete manufacturer procedure transcription in locally retrieved public-mirror HTML.
factsChecked: Original Test H C05F4:00 identifies plausibility; induced harness noise or PTU/driveshaft/RDU mechanical fault are source-listed possibilities.
Hall-effect frequency behavior accurately explained without invented speed threshold.
H1 routes C05F4 directly to H7 loose-connections/loose-sensor checks, unlike C05F0/C05F1/C05F3 electrical checks starting H2.
Conditional sensor decision and full professional verification retained; approximately 9 V H2 check is not misapplied to performance branch.

limitations: Bounded sample; no full-batch certification, hands-on diagnostic validation or vehicle fitment certification.
Public mirrors reproduce manufacturer workshop content; none is represented as manufacturer hosting.
Shared manifests, source partitions and other writers output are not directly edited.
